newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU tables new offer for telecoms open trade pact.
newsitem.headline: EU tables new offer for telecoms open trade pact.

text.p: The European Union tabled a new offer on Tuesday to open up its telecommunications market under a World Trade Organisation (WTO) pact and confirmed Spain would liberalise all its telecom services by January 1998.
EU negotiator Karl-Fredrik Falkenberg told a news conference he expected the United States -- which baulked at a global deal in April -- would shortly file a new offer in WTO discussions.
"We are trying to create momentum in the negotiations, and hope our other partners will join us in tabling improved offers," he said.

The move, which came amid high-level negotiations aimed at getting a WTO deal bringing in the United States completed by next February 15, followed talks between officials of the two top trade powers in Chicago at the weekend.
Under the EU offer, foreign investment restrictions in Spain and Belgium and indirect restrictions in France which were included in the earlier Brussels package were withdrawn.

But Falkenberg said the offer was conditional on getting significant improvements from other WTO members in the talks. The EU wanted better terms from Canada and Japan as well as from developing countries like Singapore, Korea and Brazil.
